cohort: The study examined 491,998 trials of labour among parturients in the U.S. with one previous livebirth by caesarean delivery and no previous vaginal births, excluding multiple pregnancies and births with congenital abnormalities.
finding: The risk of uterine rupture progressively decreases as the interpregnancy interval increases until approximately 21 months, after which it stabilizes.
mod_finding: Induced or augmented labours were associated with a significantly higher odds of uterine rupture (OR 2.51) compared with spontaneous labours.
birth_weight: Heavier birthweight was associated with uterine rupture.
gest_age: More advanced gestational age (from 35 to 43 weeks) was associated with uterine rupture.
